title: Trump Says He May Lower Tariffs on Canada to Other Countries' Levels (Q&A)
title_cn: 特朗普表示他可能会将加拿大的关税降低至其他国家的水平（问答）
summary: President Trump told reporters that he may lower tariffs on Canada to a level consistent with other countries, after earlier Bloomberg reporting that the US is set to halve tariffs on Canadian exports of steel and aluminum. President Trump said that he has a 'very nice relationship' with Canadian leadership right now as the two countries settle on a trade deal. The president also discussed the AI industry, telling reporters that he is planning to meet with 'AI people' next week. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Trump Asks Congress to Pass Crypto Bill Alongside Executives
title_cn: 特朗普要求国会与高管一起通过加密货币法案
summary: President Donald Trump pressed Congress to pass digital asset market structure legislation that is a top priority for the industry, as he hosted cryptocurrency executives at the White House on Wednesday.

title: Trump, Carney Optimistic on Trade Deal | Radio Balance of Power: Early Edition 8/19/2026
title_cn: 特朗普和卡尼对贸易协议持乐观态度无线电力量平衡：早期版 2026 年 8 月 19 日
summary: On the early edition of Balance of Power, Bloomberg Washington Correspondent Kailey Leinz discusses trade negotiations between the US and Cananda. On today's show, former US Ambassador to Poland Daniel Fried, Push Digital Group Vice President T.W. Arrighi, former Obama White House Special Assistant Allison Jaslow and former New Jersey Governor Chris Christie. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Peltola’s Strength in Alaska Boosts Democratic Hopes for Senate
title_cn: 佩尔托拉在阿拉斯加的实力增强了民主党对参议院的希望
summary: Mary Peltola’s strong showing in Alaska’s Senate primary is bolstering Democratic hopes that the party can defeat a two-term Republican incumbent — and possibly help it retake both houses of Congress.

title: Voter Registration, Data 'Not a Federal Issue,' Says Former Governor Chris Christie
title_cn: 前州长克里斯克里斯蒂表示，选民登记和数据“不是联邦问题”
summary: Former Governor of New Jersey Chris Christie said that issues around voting registration and administering elections should be left up to states and does not see evidence from recent years that the federal government would run elections better than Governors in individual states.  Christie, who is now a strategic advisor to the American Gaming Association, also weighed in on prediction market regulation and said that he is glad prediction market executives were left out of a White House meeting because they are 'illegal actors.'  (Source: Bloomberg)
